transactionAndPrivilegeDesign.oneTransaction: Existing restricted kernel Database.transaction establishes tenant/epoch/containment locks; no second engine/HTTP/saga. Ledger/advisory idempotency lock -> current kernel grant -> business project -> public project -> subject mapping -> active user -> membership -> selected Workspace -> selected Workload locks; maintain same identity-lock sequence as Control.grant/business_auth.permission. Re-read and hold versions/status/spec after lock. New Run has no concurrent existing execution locks. Event/outbox and ledger result commit in this same transaction; any failure rolls back all rows.
transactionAndPrivilegeDesign.actor: Trusted authenticated route writes verified subject into transaction-local inv.first_workspace_subject; helper accepts NO actor/user/risk/grant argument and derives current mapped active user. Existing tenant GUC is required and not modified by helper. A SQL-capable inv_kernel credential remains a trusted service boundary, as in existing inv.user_id based functions; it is not a user credential and no browser can set GUCs. Wrong/missing tenant/subject or disabled/unlinked mapping is denied inside helper too.
transactionAndPrivilegeDesign.migration: One new append-only Alembic revision after existing0067 plus one corresponding inv SQL resource; never change old migrations. Dedicated inv_first_workspace_writer NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT; no runtime granted membership. Own two SECURITY DEFINER functions append_first_workspace_intent and append_first_workspace_run; fixed SET search_path=pg_catalog, fully qualified every object; SET row_security=on. REVOKE ALL EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC and inv_app, GRANT EXECUTE only inv_kernel. No helper/schema/table ownership grants to runtime; no LOGIN or credential creation.
transactionAndPrivilegeDesign.minimalPrivileges: Writer USAGE inv/public; column-specific SELECT and UPDATE(lock_sentinel/kernel_lock_sentinel) only on authorization/selected context rows it locks; column-specific INSERT only public.workloads, public.runs, inv.runs, inv.business_runs. No UPDATE/DELETE business content/mapping grants. Existing FORCE RLS stays; add tenant-using/check policies TO writer for public tables (inv tenant policies already apply), never row_security off/BYPASSRLS. inv_kernel gains only SELECT workspace.version/node_id and workload.version needed for source observation; no direct public INSERT/mapping grant. Helpers verify current kernel/business grant intersection, selected scope, workload canonical SHA/versions and draft/mapping invariants and return only permitted records. Python canonical schema/hash/profile checks additionally enforce the serving contract; SQL helper validates closed metadata/CPU/scope/version again before insert.
transactionAndPrivilegeDesign.directCallBoundary: inv_app/unrelated roles cannot execute helper or assume writer; functions cannot insert cross-tenant or wrong-workspace mapping, accept raw userId, alter an existing Run/intent or disable RLS. inv_kernel already represents trusted authenticated service authority; direct-call tests require missing/mismatched GUC and stale/wrong context denial as well as privilege checks. No claim that a compromised SQL runtime credential is an authenticated end user.
